absent: Exact numeric encodings of mmap flags, protection bits, and task-size limits beyond the low-window bounds shown.
Layout of the trusted-boot global descriptor, firmware tables, and virtual-filesystem status records referenced but not defined here.
Locking and concurrency rules for mapping search, clock events, and cycle-counter calibration outside the shown initializers.
Details of generic helpers for mapping, cloning, sleeping, calibration, and clocksource registration owned by other dossiers.
Processor feature identifiers, register leaf numbers, and model-specific register addresses beyond the gating behavior described.
Full shutdown and trampoline entry sequences after platform handoff, including register state and return paths.
Complete error-path cleanup for heap and configuration mappings in the DMA-remapping table walk.

findings.text: Three 32-bit compatibility shims accept split high and low halves for file offsets and lengths, place the high half in the upper 32 bits of a 64-bit quantity, and forward the widened values with unchanged descriptor, mode, and flag arguments to generic range synchronization, advice, and preallocation services.

A shared status translator renders an in-kernel status record into the 32-bit user layout under a checked user-write window. It munges ownership through the current user namespace, encodes both device numbers for large values, stores the inode number twice, then copies mode with link count, ownership pair, device encoding, size, three second plus nanosecond timestamp pairs, and block size with block count. Any access setup or store failure reports a memory fault status.

Four compatibility entry points for path status, link status, descriptor status, and directory-relative status each first query the virtual filesystem for a kernel status record and on success invoke the shared translator; query errors are returned directly without translation.

The 32-bit mmap argument block holds six consecutive 32-bit unsigned members meaning in order requested address, then length, then protection, then flag word, then descriptor, and finally file offset.

The 32-bit mmap compatibility entry copies the six-word block from user space, fails on copy fault or when offset low bits violate page granularity, and otherwise forwards address with length and protection with flags plus descriptor and page-shifted offset to the common page-offset mapping service.

The 32-bit clone compatibility entry builds a kernel clone request by separating signal-number bits from the flag word into an exit-signal field, wiring parent and child identifier pointers, stack address, and thread-local value from its arguments, then invokes the generic clone implementation.

Mapping alignment policy treats huge-page files specially by using a huge-page derived mask and suppressing extra bits. For ordinary files it requires enabled personality configuration and the process randomization flag, then combines configured bits with the mask-derived permission.

An early boot parameter handler selects which personalities receive address alignment. It ignores empty input and unsupported processor families, accepts tokens for 32-bit only, 64-bit only, disabled, or both, and warns on unrecognized values.

The 64-bit mmap entry rejects file offsets whose sub-page low bits are set and otherwise forwards all arguments to the shared page-offset mapping service with the offset converted to page granularity.

Bottom-up window selection confines 64-bit callers using the low-address flag to a dedicated low window with optional randomization, while other callers start from the mmap base helper and are bounded above by the 32-bit task limit for 32-bit callers or by a 64-bit task limit chosen from the hint address.
Guard reservation for a new mapping is exactly one page when the shadow-stack attribute is present and zero otherwise.

The bottom-up unmapped-area service returns fixed hints unchanged, reuses a page-aligned caller hint only when it fits below the region end and does not overlap the next mapping gap, otherwise builds a search descriptor with length, limits, page-offset alignment, optional guard gap, and file-derived alignment adjustments before delegating to the generic search. Oversized lengths fail with out-of-memory status.

Top-down search proceeds through checks then directional search then fallback: reject oversized lengths and return fixed hints; divert low-address-flagged 64-bit requests to bottom-up; attempt masked hint reuse after validity and overlap checks; otherwise search downward from the mmap base with a low bound that can be raised above 4G and a high bound extended for large hints, applying page-offset and file alignment except for huge pages; on search failure invoke the bottom-up service.
Constrained low mappings use lower bound 0x40000000 and upper bound 0x80000000 with a randomization spread of 0x02000000.

A dedicated trusted-boot address-space descriptor reuses the initial page-table root, starts with two users and one reference, zeroed write-protect sequencing, an initialized mmap lock, an unlocked page-table spin lock, and an empty memory-list head. A global page-directory pointer caches the allocated top level.

Trusted-boot page installation walks four page-table levels allocating as needed, installs a frame with the supplied protection, releases the leaf mapping, and clears the no-execute bit on the top entry so low-address code can execute. Any allocation failure reports an error status.

Trampoline construction allocates a fresh top-level directory once, then identity-maps the trusted-boot memory extent page by page with kernel executable protection, halting the system with a diagnostic if any step fails.

Trusted-boot suspend preparation copies four power-management register descriptions field by field plus a firmware waking-vector address derived from the firmware table, records supplied control values and a 32-bit vector width, then translates sleep states so the first three are unsupported while suspend-to-RAM, hibernation, and power-off map to distinct platform shutdown types before invoking platform shutdown.

When trusted-boot support is inactive, both sleep hooks report success without action. The reduced-hardware sleep hook additionally always reports a no-device status with a warning when trusted-boot support is active.

Application-processor shutdown coordination counts dying processors, and when only one processor remains online polls the platform wait counter once per millisecond until it matches the counted value or a bounded timeout expires, warning on timeout and reporting busy status on mismatch, otherwise success.
Application-processor wait timeout is 1 second unit.
Trusted-boot serial log geometry uses base 0x60000 with size 0x8000, maximum-size field at byte offset 16, and payload start at byte offset 24.
The log identifier is sixteen bytes: first group 0x26 0x25 0x19 0xC0, next group 0x30 0x6B 0xB4 0x4D, next group 0x4C 0x84 0xA3 0xE9, final group 0x53 0xB8 0x81 0x74.

Log read maps the fixed serial region, verifies the stored identifier against the expected value, clamps the request to the stored maximum size and current file position, stages bytes through a temporary kernel buffer into user space, advances the position by the transferred count, and always unmaps before returning with fault, memory, or count status.
The log file-operations table provides a read handler for the serial-log retrieval routine and the default seeking behavior.

Late trusted-boot initialization does nothing when support is inactive; otherwise it builds the identity trampoline, resets the shutdown counter, registers a dying-processor hook, optionally exposes a read-only debug file for the log, and installs both normal and extended suspend preparation hooks.
Trusted execution register windows use public base 0xFED30000 and private base 0xFED20000; the mapped page count is the difference of those bases shifted by page size.
Heap pointer field is at offset 0x0300 and heap size field at offset 0x0308; digest length is 20 bytes.

A digest record is twenty consecutive bytes. The measured-launch data record is packed with version first, then firmware identifier digest, then flag word, then validity word, followed by three digests for init module and measured environment and monitor, then policy digest with policy control, then wakeup address with reserved word, and finally region count with region offset plus DMA-remapping count with DMA-remapping offset.

DMA-remapping table lookup returns the supplied table when trusted-boot support is inactive; otherwise it maps configuration registers to read heap base and size, maps the heap, skips three leading variable-length heap sections and a size word to reach measured-launch data, derives the protected table address from its DMA-remapping offset, and leaves the heap mapped for later use. Mapping failures yield a null result.
Profiling program-counter sampling returns the instruction address from the register frame. The legacy timer interrupt handler dispatches the global clock event and reports handled status.

Time initialization registers interrupt zero for the timer with no-balancing, poll, and timer attributes, attempts high-precision event timer enablement with programmable-interval-timer fallback before registering the interrupt, and in the late phase selects interrupt mode, initializes legacy timers, finalizes interrupt delivery mode, initializes the cycle counter, and enables a low-power delay mechanism when the corresponding processor feature is present.

Cycle-counter initialization aborts deadline-timer support when the counter feature is absent, upgrades the early calibration hook, retries frequency detection and marks the counter unstable on failure, enables scheduling-clock services and fine delay calibration, checks system reliability, aborts on unsynchronized counters, optionally disables the watchdog for reliable configurations, then registers the early clocksource and probes the always-running timer.
Secondary-processor time-conversion state is seeded by copying both conversion slots from the boot processor to every other possible processor with per-processor sequence initialization.

Always-running timer detection requires a sufficient processor identification level plus absence of virtualization, presence of nonstop and adjust features, and no asynchronous resets; it then reads frequency parameters from the timestamp-counter leaf, scales kilohertz units, rejects small denominators, samples the adjust offset, and permanently sets the corresponding capability.

Caller-visible failures include user-copy faults, misaligned offsets rejected as invalid, oversized or unplaceable mappings reported as out of memory, unsupported sleep states warned and rejected, reduced-hardware suspend reporting no device, processor-shutdown races reporting busy, trampoline mapping failures halting the system, and log mapping or allocation failures yielding fault or memory statuses.

The trusted-boot address-space descriptor carries its own mmap lock and page-table spin lock initialized at declaration time alongside reference counts and list state; page-table installation operates under that descriptor context.
Log diagnostic output uses a fixed textual prefix identifying the trusted-boot subsystem, and module state includes a single global trusted-boot pointer plus a boot-time sixteen-byte identifier.
